name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19, apprentice plasterer, Dakar
title: Evening Tea Invitation
situation: After the plastering workshop ends, Mariam, one of Aminata's roommates, catches her at the gate and says a few apprentices are going to the tea stall near the market to celebrate finishing the week's walls. Mariam asks Aminata to come along, saying it won't be late and she can still review her photos afterward. Aminata rarely joins these gatherings, preferring to go straight home to rest and study her work. She stands there, her porridge money pouch heavy against her waist, and has to decide whether to accept.

context.relationship_profiles: Aminata and Mariam share the rented room and the evening rice-and-beans routine; Mariam often jokes with her and has helped her carry tile bags, but Aminata has never told her anything about her savings or family. Aminata appreciates Mariam's lightheartedness but keeps her distance because she knows Mariam does not share her strict focus on practicing walls.
context.tendencies: When invited to after-class gatherings in the past, she has almost always declined with a polite excuse about needing rest or study, and she usually goes straight home to eat and review photos. She once joined a market outing with her roommates but left early because she felt she needed to practice a corner technique she had missed in class.
context.current_state: She is physically tired from waking at 4:30, stirring porridge, and plastering for two hours, and her back and shoulder ache from the long strokes. The cloth pouch of coins is heavy against her waist, reminding her of the day's sales, and she has not eaten since midday, so hunger is beginning to pull at her.
context.immediate_memories: Mariam's voice at the gate recalls an evening two weeks ago when Mariam coaxed her into sharing a bowl of fried plantains near the market, and she stayed later than planned, feeling drowsy the next morning during plaster practice. The sight of the metal gate also brings back the last tea-stall outing when she paid for her own cup and then spent extra on a sweet she had not intended to buy.
context.reflective_memories: She remembers her father in the village always finishing the millet harvest before joining neighbors for any celebration, and she holds the same rule for herself: work first, rest later. She also recalls evenings when she stayed in to examine her wall photos, and those nights usually led to noticeable improvements in her next practice session, while social evenings did not.
